mechanics.def_type: Fish are ordinary ThingDefs (category=Item, thingClass=ThingWithComps, thingCategories:["Fish"]), almost always ParentName-chained to an abstract base (vanilla: FishBase in Odyssey/Defs/ThingDefs_Items/Items_Resource_Fish.xml). No FishDef, no per-fish water-type field, no biome-reference field ANYWHERE on the ThingDef itself — confirmed by reading VCEF_DuskySprat's and Fish_Salmon's full field dumps: neither carries anything named biome/water/salinity/temperature.
mechanics.binding_field: BiomeDef.fishTypes — a nested dict with exactly four buckets: freshwater_Common, freshwater_Uncommon, saltwater_Common, saltwater_Uncommon. Each bucket is {defName: commonalityWeight} (vanilla weights are flat 1 — the buckets themselves carry the rarity tier, not a weight spread). A fifth key, rareCatchesSetMaker, points to a ThingSetMakerDef (e.g. RareFishingCatches_Cold) for the occasional non-fish rare catch.
mechanics.implication_for_this_task: Fish placement per water is BIOME work, not def work. A fish ThingDef is completely reusable across any biome's fishTypes list — the same Fish_Salmon def could legally sit in ten different BiomeDefs' saltwater_Common bucket with zero edits to the def. So the only reason to write a NEW fish ThingDef is when no existing def clears the recognizability bar for a given water's register — never because an existing, passing def is somehow 'bound' elsewhere. The freshwater/saltwater split is the only chemistry Odyssey's own mechanism understands; brine/lethal/pollution/milk-pond flavor (this campaign's water-kinds taxonomy) has no engine hook at all — it is pure flavor text on top of freshwater or saltwater, same as every other biome's fishTypes block already is.
verified_against: ThingDef.json field dump of Fish_Salmon and VCEF_DuskySprat

weeping_stones.roster_ruling_verbatim: YES — fish live in the true pools: the biome's §4 law is 'reliable standing fresh water' with pilgrimage density, the pools are breeding/ritual grounds (§4 truce), and a dead-silent pool is the sheet's image of a DEAD oasis (§10b). Water is map-scale (world-scale water 0, §0) so fish ride the pool terrain, not world water.
weeping_stones.water_chemistry: freshwater, standing, sacred/truce — hard constraints from the sheet: nothing pollution-flavored (no tumorfish, §10 sacrilege), nothing that turns the pool into a hunting story (§6 ambush-at-water ban)
